note: Set A is slightly better because it has fewer internal contradictions between claimed values and their supporting quotes compared to Set B. Both sets suffer from significant duplication (stating the same fact twice with different quotes) and fail to extract the state-space matrix definitions ($A_d, B_d, C_d, D_d$) which are prominent in the text. Set B introduces more invented values (e.g., -72 deg, -12.5 dB) that directly contradict the text in their own quotes (e.g., quoting '-75' but claiming '-72').
remarks: Both sets miss the engineering definitions of the discrete-time matrices ($A_d, B_d, C_d, D_d$) found in the text. Both sets hallucinate multiple conflicting values for the same graph points (e.g. phase at 1.00 Hz is claimed as -75, -80, -72 across the sets). Set B relies more heavily on the figure caption as a quote for specific data points, which is vague.
